I will keep the land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. I am in southern Hebei on the North China Plain, so this rotation fits my climate, my irrigation conditions, and the way I manage labor. Because I am educated and I want stable output more than experimentation, I will use better-performing seed rather than traditional seed, keep fertilizer rates moderate but complete, irrigate only at the key growth stages, and avoid excessive pesticide sprays. I will prepare the wheat ground with rotary tillage after maize harvest residue is handled, then after wheat harvest I will move quickly into summer maize with no delay. For wheat, I will focus on stand establishment, one strong basal fertilizer program, a few key irrigations, and disease control only when pressure is real. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen higher than wheat, and manage weeds and insects tightly early because that is where yield is decided. I am assuming I am planning 20 mu of the same land through a full wheat-maize double-cropping year.
